newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher but lag Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher but lag Dow rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended higher on Tuesday, but lagged behind a rally in New York as weak gold stocks restrained Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 11.72 points to close at 5565.08 in heavy turnover of 94.5 million shares worth C$1.47 billion ($1.09 billion).
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained nearly 35 points to close at about 6007.
"The Canadian market lagged behind today. Gold prices are down and that has hampered the performance," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser at Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd.
A sharp rally in Canadian bonds and positive news in some sectors pushed 12 of 14 sub-groups higher.

Canada's 9.00 percent long bond closed up 1.53 at 110.30, Weaker-than-expected U.S employment cost data released earlier today calmed wage inflation fears and pushed North American bond markets higher.
Toronto's gains were partly offset by a 178-point loss in the heavily weighted gold group. COMEX gold futures were hit by fund and trade selling today.
* Paper stocks added 82 points, extending a recent rally.

Avenor Inc. rose 0.95 to 23.50, while Abitibi-Price Inc. climbed 0.60 to 18.75. Stone Consolidated Corp. improved 0.55 to 16.10. The sector has gained recently on data which showed newsprint inventories are falling.
* Inmet Mining Corp. fell 1.15 to 8.35 on 2.9 million shares after it took huge writedowns in its third quarter earnings.
* Edper Group receipts topped the volume list, climbing 1.25 to 69.25 on 20.7 million shares.
* Independent investment dealer Midland Walwyn Inc. eased 0.05 to 11.70.
Midland, the subject of recent takeover rumors, asserted today it is not for sale and said a hostile bid is unlikely.
